item.title: Bond Traders on Edge as Risks of Fed Rate Hike This Week Mount
item.description: Bond traders enter the week seeing a better than one-in-three chance that the Federal Reserve hikes interest rates on Wednesday after flaring Middle East tensions lifted oil prices, boosting inflation worries and yields.

item.title: Fed Faces Growing Pressure to Hike Rates as Price Risks Rebound
item.description: Federal Reserve officials will head into their policy meeting this week confronting a resurgence in price pressures that could make their decision on whether to hold or hike interest rates a close call — and a contentious one.

item.title: European SpaceX Rival in Talks to Raise $300 Million, FT Reports
item.description: The Exploration Company Gmbh, a potential European rival to Elon Musk’s SpaceX, is in talks to raise at least $300 million, in part from the European Union’s Scaleup Europe Fund, bumping the company’s valuation to more than $2 billion, the Financial Times reported.

item.title: US Presses Mexico to Mirror Its Steel Tariff Wall Aimed at China
item.description: The US has asked Mexico to mirror Washington’s tariff wall against Chinese steel and aluminum by imposing Section 232-style duties on imports from outside North America, according to four people with direct knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Apple Glasses May Debut at WWDC 2027: Privacy, Camera Features Versus Meta
item.description: Company debated whether glasses will be able to record video.

item.title: Traders Are Getting a New Tool to Wager on the Biggest US Stocks
item.description: Investors will soon have another way to bet on the hottest stocks from Nvidia Corp. to SpaceX, without trading a single share.

item.title: Trump’s Section 301 Tariffs: How They’re Being Challenged in Court
item.description: This time, it was only hours after President Donald Trump’s latest global tariffs took effect before they became the subject of a legal challenge. His administration is once again accused of abusing US trade law to the detriment of American businesses and consumers.

item.title: Big Tech Earnings Slam Into a Market in Revolt Over AI Spending
item.description: For years, US technology giants had a tacit agreement with investors: The companies could spend lavishly on artificial intelligence, and the stock market would reward them long as their revenues were rising. That deal is suddenly breaking down.

item.title: Brazil ETF Market Triples in Boom for New Latin America Funds
item.description: Exchange-traded funds are cropping up at a fast clip in local markets across Latin America as investors flock to a swath of new products tailored to domestic demand.

item.title: India Says US Trade Talks Helped It Secure an Export Advantage
item.description: India said trade negotiations with the US have helped place it in the “lower tier” of additional tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump’s administration, allowing the country to secure an advantage for key exports.

item.title: Modi Punctured as Awakened India Students Force Swift Retreat
item.description: For much of Narendra Modi’s 12 years ruling India, he’s looked nearly unbeatable at the polls. This weekend he swiftly yielded to a group that didn’t exist a few months ago, energizing opponents who have struggled to gain traction against one of the nation’s most powerful leaders.

item.title: Barrick Evacuates Chile Workers by Helicopter After Storm
item.description: Barrick Mining Corp. said it safely evacuated workers who had been stranded in their Barriales camp in northern Chile after severe storms blocked road access.

item.title: Australian Prime Minister Albanese to Press Trump on New Tariffs
item.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he will appeal directly to President Donald Trump over new tariffs announced by Washington, describing the levies as unjustified.

item.title: Memory Frenzy Primes China Champion CXMT for Historic Debut
item.description: Investor excitement over the memory chip trade is setting outsize expectations for the Shanghai debut of CXMT Corp., which is on the brink of making history after a near-record initial public offering.

item.title: Iraq to Sign Agreement with Syria on Building of Oil Pipelines
item.description: Iraq will sign an agreement with Syria on the construction of pipelines linking oil production sites to global export markets via the Mediterranean, according to a statement.

item.title: Fed, Bank of England, Bank of Japan Face $100 Oil Inflation Test
item.description: From Washington to London to Tokyo, central bankers are set to reveal just how worried they are about a return of oil to about $100 a barrel.

item.title: DeepSeek Said to Tell Backers of Funding Pause After Viral Posts
item.description: DeepSeek has told prospective investors in its second fundraising round that it’s suspending the deal for now, people familiar with the matter said, days after comments widely attributed to founder Liang Wenfeng about US-Chinese AI competition went viral.

item.title: The ‘Trump Trade’ Is Turning Into a Loser in the Stock Market
item.description: When Donald Trump was elected to a second term as president, amateur and professional traders alike rushed to identify which stocks would benefit from his aggressive economic policies.

item.title: Austin’s Mayor Tackles Housing Affordability, and Canada Faces New Tariffs
item.description: Former trade negotiator says don’t underestimate Canada’s ire

item.title: Heat Bakes Central US, Raising Energy Demand as East Stays Cool
item.description: Baking temperatures will sear the central US from the Rocky Mountains to the Mississippi River and eventually push down into the Gulf Coast for the rest of the month, putting regional power grids to the test.

item.title: Big Tech Debt Flood Is Taking Over Risk In Market: Credit Weekly
item.description: Big Tech’s insatiable appetite for AI investment is unleashing a relentless wave of bond sales — and having a bigger impact on the US corporate bond market than might be obvious.

item.title: South Africa’s Vanishing Aspirations to Lead Africa: New Economy
item.description: The image of “Afrophobia” spurred by expulsions and protests is harming the country’s image.

item.title: Ukraine Seeks 30-Year Energy Pact With Canada, Minister Says
item.description: Ukraine is looking to sign a 30-year strategic energy agreement with Canada and proposing an “energy security bridge” focused on the supply of Canadian LNG, Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said.

item.title: Charting the Global Economy: Growth Picks Up, AI Boom Continues
item.description: Applications for US unemployment benefits fell last week to an almost 60-year low, adding to signs of a stable labor market that will allow the Federal Reserve to focus on inflation.

item.title: Saudi Arabia-Bound Supertanker U-Turns Before Houthi Chokepoint
item.description: A Hong Kong-flagged supertanker bound for Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea port of Yanbu has U-turned just before reaching the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint, where recent attacks were launched by the Houthis as part of a blockade on ships linked to the kingdom.

item.title: Bordeaux Suburbs at Risk as 200,000 Flee Fires in France, Spain
item.description: More than 200,000 people fled towns in central Spain and southern France overnight as uncontrolled wildfires moved ever closer to the cities of Madrid and Bordeaux.

item.title: India’s Modi Adopts Reels Amid Instagram-Fueled Student Unrest
item.description: As student protests spread across India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has turned to Meta Platforms Inc.’s Instagram Reels, swapping his trademark cinematic videos for raw, self-recorded messages aimed at the country’s youth.

item.title: Europe’s Stock Market Rally Is the Most Concentrated in Years
item.description: The European equity market has long been seen as immune to shocks driven by only a handful of stocks. A narrow rally in 2026 has completely flipped that script.

item.title: Samsung Inks $200 Billion Chip Supply with Broadcom
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. won a contract worth more than $200 billion to make chips for Broadcom Inc., as the companies race to win a larger share of the AI infrastructure market.

item.title: Indonesia Arrests Former Top Graft Prosecutor After Police Raids
item.description: Indonesia’s former top graft prosecutor was arrested on suspicion of money laundering, weeks after police raids uncovered $26 million worth of gold bars and cash at a house he owns.
